matches.rationale: The ground truth says Theorem 2.3's proof replaces true complex conjugation with a mere order-2 swap of Hodge components, which only coincides with conjugation when the component is 1-dimensional and fails for larger components. Findings 2, 9 and 6 independently catch the symptom of this conflation (equalities between swapped Hodge classes stated without the required complex-conjugate bar, in the proof of Theorem 2.3 and in the downstream Example 2.4), and finding 10 explicitly demonstrates the dimension-dependent breakdown in Corollary 2.7 (formula correct only when |I_m| is not greater than 1), matching the core mechanism described in the ground truth even though it surfaces in a different passage (permitted by R3).

pred_verdicts.rationale: Targets a claimed contradiction in the introduction's comparison isomorphism, an unrelated and unverified notational point not tied to the Theorem 2.3 defect in ground truth.
Identifies a missing complex-conjugate bar in the proof of Theorem 2.3, directly exposing the swap-vs-conjugation conflation that is the core mechanism of the ground-truth defect.
Points to a Poincaré-duality normalization error (P vs P^{-1}) in Section 2.4 that is a distinct technical issue not described by the ground truth.
Flags a factor-of-i error in the real-subspace formula (w, iw vs (v-v̄)/2i), a separate normalization slip not matching the dimension-generality mechanism in ground truth.
Reports a Poincaré-dual coefficient (Q vs Q^{-1}) issue in the proof, a distinct computational point unrelated to the swap/conjugation conflation described in ground truth.
Shows that omitting a complex conjugate in the μ formula trivializes the result, the same missing-conjugation symptom underlying the Theorem 2.3 defect.
Notes a floor-function/typo issue in index selection, a separate notational slip not addressing the general-dimension failure described in ground truth.
Points out that the stated basis only spans the charge-zero part of an infinite-dimensional ring, a distinct imprecision unrelated to the Theorem 2.3 mechanism.
Identifies that the pairing C(φ_C(U_k), φ_C(U_k)) should use the conjugate of φ_C(U_k), the same conjugation-omission symptom that manifests the Theorem 2.3 defect.

Explicitly computes that the real-dimension formula in Corollary 2.7 only matches when |I_m| equals 1 and fails for larger |I_m|, directly confirming the ground truth's stated dimension-dependent failure.
